name: Traditional Cel Animation
visualIdentity: A historical 2D drawing technique, distinct from cel-shaded 3D. Use fixed backgrounds, layered character drawings, consistent linework, flat fills, hard shadow shapes, distinct poses, and clean transparent compositing. Digital work should be described as a cel-animation simulation; physical cels are unspecified.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to character-led scenes on simple backgrounds, mascots, anime, cartoons, storybooks, and expressive characters in product or explainer scenes. It can also support title sequences and nostalgic narratives. These are stated fit examples, not guarantees for every subject.
limitations: Needs readable artwork and suitable layers or a rig for facial motion. Avoid target-following that distorts faces or distracts. It does not itself specify exact pose rate, palette, or audio. Do not imply photographed physical cels or validated physics from a digital simulation.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Preserve task, brand, reference, and asset colors and their role assignments. An optional new-artwork example uses background #F6EDD8, foreground #263746, accent_1 #718E9D, accent_2 #BE795F; these are suggestions, not style requirements. Keep colors discrete: gradients are disabled. The accent/foreground pairs have contrast ratios 3.528 and 3.546, below the 4.5 normal-text target; use accents decoratively and verify actual compositing. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Animate with distinct drawings and held poses; preserve exposure cadence and do not automatically interpolate poses. Motion should be time-driven, seekable, and deterministic for video; delivery frame rate may exceed drawing exposure rate. Optional fits include bounded pupil following when facial layers support it, and story or chapter states with readable holds. Interactive HTML may map pointer or scroll to those states, with neutral gaze recovery, reversible transitions, and reduced-motion behavior where applicable; video must not depend on live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence to suit the task and honor supplied choices. Synchronize audio with picture, preserve speech intelligibility, avoid clipping, and inspect the final mix.
assetRequirements: Prepare fixed backgrounds and layered character drawings or numbered, transparent frame sequences with consistent dimensions and clear naming. Krita is a suggested drawing and PNG-sequence tool. Inspect assets before composition. Optional facial tracking needs suitable eye layers or a rig; digital appearance does not establish physical production.
combinations: Use alone for character-led scenes on simple backgrounds. Optional hybrid: style-039 matte gouache plates behind flat-fill characters; keep plate colors subordinate and avoid painted character texture or mixing oil and gouache. Or style-101 restrained multiplane parallax for depth; preserve layer order, crop margins, ground contact, and avoid exposed edges or calling it full 3D. These are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Choose drawing/rendering and motion methods by style, action, assets, and fidelity; assign one owner per animated property. Krita prepares drawings; optional PixiJS renders layered 2D artwork and GSAP can provide a paused, seekable timeline. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and record why; an existing React project alone is insufficient. Pipeline tools do not replace style-specific drawing or motion. Inspect key frames and the decoded video.
